authorities.title: SEC Plain Writing Initiative
authorities.mechanism: Clear, concise, well-organized writing appropriate to audience; SEC points to concrete plain-English practices.
authorities.engine_use: Prefer concrete verbs, short decision-relevant sentences, tables/bullets for complex records, and clarity over ornamental legalese.
authorities.limitation: Disclosure-writing authority, not a universal rule for every legal communication.

authorities.title: A Plain English Handbook
authorities.mechanism: Active voice and strong verbs reduce ambiguity and hidden agency.
authorities.engine_use: Flag vague passive constructions when actor/owner matters; do not ban passive voice mechanically.
authorities.limitation: Old but still maintained as an SEC writing resource.

authorities.title: DOJ Principles of Federal Prosecution of Business Organizations — Attorney-Client and Work Product Protections
authorities.mechanism: Privilege protects legal-advice communications; business facts and ordinary business communications are distinct from legal advice.
authorities.engine_use: Do not infer privilege from lawyer involvement or a label; keep legal-advice purpose and distribution context explicit when privilege matters.
authorities.limitation: Federal prosecution guidance, not a jurisdiction-neutral privilege treatise.

authorities.title: Federal Rules of Evidence — Rule 408 context
authorities.mechanism: Compromise protections turn on disputed claims, compromise context and purpose; Rule 408 does not make every settlement-tagged statement unusable for every purpose.
authorities.engine_use: Require disputed-claim and compromise-purpose context before recommending settlement labels; never promise automatic protection.
authorities.limitation: Federal evidence rule; state, arbitral and cross-border regimes can differ.

authorities.title: FIDIC claims guidance and FAQs
authorities.mechanism: Timely notice, contemporaneous records and substantiation preserve decision-quality evidence around project claims.
authorities.engine_use: For major-project letters, separate event, notice/record, causation, effect, mitigation and requested instruction.
authorities.limitation: Contract edition and amended particular conditions control; never infer a notice period without reading the governing contract.

authorities.title: AACE Recommended Practice 29R-03 — Forensic Schedule Analysis
authorities.mechanism: Critical-path/delay analysis requires a disciplined method; occurrence of an event alone does not prove project delay causation.
authorities.engine_use: Flag project letters that leap from event to entitlement without a stated causation/schedule-effect bridge.
authorities.limitation: Recommended practice, expressly not a prescriptive legal standard.

authorities.title: 2026 SEC-filed merger negotiation record involving DLA Piper and Sullivan & Cromwell
authorities.mechanism: Public deal history shows sophisticated negotiations decomposed into funding obligations, closing conditions, no-shop scope, recommendation-change rights, termination fees, covenants and dissenters' rights rather than generic fairness rhetoric.
authorities.engine_use: Deal strategy should express agreed/open items, risk allocation, conditionality, decision authority and linked trade space.
authorities.limitation: One transaction record; do not imitate named counsel or treat deal-specific positions as universal market terms.

authorities.title: Freshfields — Deal implications for 2026
authorities.mechanism: Modern deal terms explicitly allocate regulatory timing, efforts, remedy and break-fee risk under uncertainty.
authorities.engine_use: When drafting deal correspondence, distinguish commercial principle from risk allocation and execution certainty.
authorities.limitation: Firm publication and market commentary, not governing law.
